Footnote letters from the printed page have been omitted throughout. Line 2: 'quo in loco ... a aut plene dixerim' is obscure and may be corrupt; rendered tentatively. Line 4: 'quai' read as 'quia'. Line 5: the text gives Abraham's 60th year for his departure, but later his 70th; and 'anni Sem 78' conflicts with Shem being 100 two years after the flood (98 expected) — the numerals may be corrupt. Line 6: '350 years' in Egypt as the opponents' figure is as printed; the author's own figure is 210.

VII: 'IIIa 646' read as 3646. 'inibi captivitatis tempora' taken as 'times of captivity there'. IX: the sense of the sentence ending 'sunt anni 111' is obscure (561 − 450 = 111); '[fewer]' supplied. 'Godolias' stands where Athaliah's 6 years would fall; 'Amos' read as Amon; the second 'Joachim' (3 months 20 days) taken as Jehoiachin. X: the citation 'Dan. XI' should be Dan. 9; 'III decima' read as 'decima'. VIII: 'Cufarsamoth' is evidently a variant of Cushan-rishathaim; 'Sebon' is probably Ibzan; the 'son' of Gideon is Abimelech. XII: 'a 62 hebdomadas Dominum' seems corrupt. XIII: the words 'monis ad respondendum' appear to be a stray intrusion (cf. 'sermonis ad respondendum' in Daniel) and are rendered as [...]; Persian king names (Argus, Socidanus, Artabus, Olus, Arser) are kept as given; the list is historically confused.

XIV: 'feminino aspernamento' (lit. 'womanish contempt') is odd and may be corrupt. XVI: the reference 'I Cor. X, 15' is the edition's; the verse is 1 Cor. 10:11. 'Septimo et millesimo anno' is rendered literally as 'thousand-and-seventh year'; the context requires the seventh millennium (the start of the 7000th year count). XVII: the 369 years to the consulship of Caesarius and Atticus (AD 397) imply a passion date of AD 28; the citation 'II Thess. II, 8, 4' covers vv. 3–4 and 8. XVIII: 'donec consummentur anni tres; qui anni tres' is translated as 'until the years are completed; and these years', omitting 'tres' ('three'), which seems to be an error for the thousand years ('mille'); the reading is uncertain.

nodes.text: THE CHRONOLOGY OF QUINTUS JULIUS HILARIANUS, OR LITTLE BOOK ON THE DURATION OF THE WORLD.

I. However long the mind of anyone who fears God has been intent on the divine laws, so much will he learn to choose what is true, so that by learning he is made wise, because the guide of the eyes of his heart in the law is Christ, the power of God the Father and [his] wisdom (1 Cor. 1:24). And, as though the doors of heaven had been opened, he rejoices as if he had heard from God's own mouth, when he learns something truly wise in the law. Hence the wisdom of God does not allow a man to keep silent; he is compelled (truth itself constraining him) to speak, so that he may make others wise. But one who is joined to wisdom cannot be envious. Therefore the wise man wishes (through the wisdom of God by which he was made wise), having abandoned envy, through which death holds sway and reigns (Wis. 2:24), that all men in the world should be wise. For he knows that it was foretold in the law that the multitude of the wise is the health of the whole world (Wis. 6:26). So when, with wisdom as guide, there was a discussion from the law in the presence of the brethren, and the objection was raised by them that the beginning of the world and its end cannot be known by us at all, since some assert that the world is already more than 20,000 years old; others refuse to grant it a beginning and an end; others (granting a beginning) have held that it will be eternal. To this I say: to establish this by art is the philosophy of the world and empty deceit; they have loved, and are lovers of, the display of words and of opinion rather than the truth. For if we listen to the command of God, which is faithful, we must accept whatever the divine law has faithfully related to us; and this, with the Lord's consent (if you permit), will be simply related to you. For there are those who think that the years in the law were written down idly or superfluously, as though not of necessity, not knowing that such people have little faith, who do not believe that what the law of God makes known is true. But they said: Is it a great thing to bring forth something from the law and commit it to writing? Truly, I said: for, as you yourselves know, long ago, at your urging, I wrote on the reckoning of Easter and the number of the years of the world; but I kept silent for some time for this reason, that these little works should not be composed by us irrationally with the seasonings of an alien wisdom. Therefore, having arranged matters better, we have already sent ahead a little book on the most holy day of Easter, in which we also demonstrated according to the law which is the first month; and next, in this little work, we set down by reckoning, each in its proper order, the course of the years from the making of the world.

II. At these promises, then, the brethren, much pleased, do what we laid down quite carefully. For very many have written on this matter not consistently but variously, so that the reader's mind, left in doubt, cannot know what is truer. I will do as you wish, as I myself promised, with the Lord God Christ, that is, showing [the way]. Therefore I will go through all the parts and rules of the years skilfully and with some care, so that the exposition itself may seem to readers, as to those walking, a delightful road, even and level. After the various compilations of earlier writers (especially those that are already held as settled opinion), to say anything is wicked or proud; but I will say it, for reason compels it of necessity, though I believe it is not proud if at a later time something better is brought forth from the law by anyone. This too the holy apostle Paul, counselling peace, testifies and says: If something better has been revealed to another sitting by, let the first be silent (1 Cor. 14:30). And the apostle certainly said this about any disputation on the law: on whatever matter, however anyone has thought, so that, as he has thought, and rightly, the better may be admitted. Now the reckoning turns on the complete number of the years, where no one can put an incomplete number for the complete one, or go beyond the complete number itself, and establish as true what is less than or more than the complete number. So let us now come to the matter and relate everything in its order, and let it be understood at what point, wishing to attain this reckoning, I may have spoken fully.

III. When, then, this world was established by God the Creator, and he saw that all things had appeared at his command out of nothing, early came the heaven with its adornments, that is, the sun, the moon and the stars, shining with light for the changes and signs of the seasons; the earth, full of green, with every kind of seed brought to completion, having flowers of different colours in a divine painting; the seas, hemmed in by the enclosure of shores and mountains so that they should not pass over, as if besieged by a kind of rampart, and having in themselves from there the motion first brought forth, and every living soul. After this completion of the world, then, it pleased almighty God to set up man, whom almighty God wished to be something above the other animals: for those he created by his command and word; this one he fashioned with his holy hands (Gen. 1:27), and set him, free and lord, over all his works: those, to be ruled by him; him, so that as a wise, rational and shrewd animal he might govern himself in the world. From his time, then, and that of those after him, we show the generations of all (running through them) down to our own age: how many years it is since this world in which we live was made, which, however, according to the Gospel's word, is already set at its end. We hold the origin of this world to be from the eighth day before the Kalends of April [25 March], on which it was begun and made, as we have already set out by running reckoning in the little book on Easter; and we related that the world was without man for five days, and that on the sixth day [man] was fashioned and given life by the breath of God.

IV. From the birth of the first-formed, that is Adam, to the flood that took place under Noah, there are 2257 years, which are faithfully verified generation by generation thus. Adam in his 230th year begot Seth. Seth in [his] 205th begot Enos. Enos in his 170th year begot Cainan. Cainan in his 170th year begot Malalehel. Malalehel in his 165th year begot Jared. Jared in his 162nd year begot Enoch. Enoch in his 165th year begot Methuselah. Methuselah in his 182nd year begot Lamech. Here the early years of Methuselah, which a copyists' error produced, no one has noticed, no one has examined, no one has corrected by careful inquiry: [they say] that he had lived 167 years and begot Lamech, and afterwards lived 811 years, which cannot be true, because 811 is shown to run past the flood, being 14 years too many. For no one escaped the flood; no one lived through it apart from the ark. Therefore Methuselah lived 182 years and then begot Lamech, and after this lived 787 years; for so the true faith of divine Scripture shows, which related that Methuselah both lived and died before the flood.

V. Lamech in his 188th year begot Noah; for in the six-hundredth year of Noah the flood took place and was completed. From the time of the flood to the 60th year of Abraham, in which he set out from his land on his sojourning, there are 1012 years. In order thus: the second generations are shown, from Shem the son of Noah. But because Shem's 78 years were completed at the end of the flood, 2 years are clearly needed for the reckoning of the total which we have marked out after the flood: for Shem himself, two years after the flood, was 100 years old, and then begot Arphaxad; those who wrote out this reckoning did not put these 2 years into the number of years, since they did not foresee them at all. So after the flood Shem lived 2 years and begot Arphaxad. Arphaxad in his 135th year begot Salah. Salah in his 130th year begot Eber. Eber in his 134th year begot Peleg. Peleg in his 130th year begot Reu. Reu in his 132nd year begot Serug. Serug in his 130th year begot Nahor. Nahor in his 79th year begot Terah. Terah in his 70th year begot Abram. Abram in his 70th year set out from his land (as we said) to Haran. From Abraham's sojourning to the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt into the desert there are 430 years. These are then set out more surely by us as follows.

VI. Abraham sojourned 30 years and received Isaac, the son of the promise. When he had desired to hear the word of the Lord as to when his seed might inherit the land of Canaan, having prepared a sacrifice, at evening the Lord spoke to him, concluding and at the same time indicating that his seed would still sojourn in the land of Canaan and in servitude to the Egyptians for 400 years, as divine Scripture testifies to Abraham himself in the book of Genesis: Knowing, you shall know how your seed will be a stranger in a land not its own, and they will be reduced to servitude, and [others] will rule over them for 400 years. But the nation which they serve I will judge (Gen. 15:13–14). And therefore the most wise lawgiver Moses, with our God as author, following [this], says thus: Now the dwelling of the children of Israel, in which they dwelt in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, they and their fathers, was 430 years (Exod. 12:40). Paying too little attention to this, the disputers of the years have vainly stated that the children of Israel were in Egypt only 350 years, and not the full 430. For, as more fully, so better, we show by running through their generations that the 430 years were completed by the seed of Abraham, from the birth of Isaac to their departure from Egypt (not in the land of Egypt alone, but in the land of Canaan). Isaac in his 60th year begot Jacob. Jacob, when he was 130 years old, entered Egypt with his sons and grandsons and all his offspring, among which grandsons was Kohath son of Levi, who is the grandfather of Moses: so Amram was born in Egypt. Amram begot Moses; in his 80th year this Moses went out of Egypt with the children of Israel; and accordingly they dwelt in the land of Canaan from the birth of Isaac to Jacob's entry into Egypt 140 years, and in Egypt they spent 210 years. This is enough to clarify these years, about which very many who had spoken of them were in doubt.

VII. And so from the making of the world to the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt there are 3646 years. They were in the desert 40 years; then, Moses having died, Joshua son of Nun brought the peoples across the bed of the Jordan dry-shod to the land of promise; and, with the divine favour on their side, he subdued the fierce nations and judged as a just man. Under the Judges, moreover, there were in that land times of captivity, from Joshua son of Nun to Samuel the prophet, who anointed Saul king, over 561 years. But so that readers may recognise both that our total has been gathered in full and that the apostle Paul stated it rightly in the Acts of the Apostles, [namely] that, the land of Canaan having been thus divided to our fathers by Joshua son of Nun, the Lord God gave them judges for 450 years until Samuel the prophet: for the apostle Paul in the Acts of the Apostles was dealing with another matter and urging another point; he named not the times of captivity as well, but only those in which they had judges and held dominion. 'And he gave them judges,' he says (Acts 13:20). For when they were handed over into captivity for their sins they did not have their own Judges, but were oppressed by foreigners. Nor indeed could the apostle Paul himself go against the faith of the Scripture of the book of Judges, had he wished to run through the length of the times. He named the judges given by God to the people because he wished to commend faith in the Lord Christ; for he addressed the people as far as David, in order to tell how Christ came from his seed, in whom, he preached, believers (if they would) would have forgiveness of sins.

VIII. These times of the judges, then, are shown thus. Joshua son of Nun judged with the elders for 30 years. After this, when they sinned, they were handed over to Cushan-rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia, for eight years; and the Lord raised up Othniel to help them, who, having killed Cufarsamoth, judged Israel for 50 years. After him, when they sinned, they served Eglon king of Moab for 18 years. Ehud killed Eglon, and Ehud judged for 80 years. When he died, the people sinned, and they served Jabin king of the Canaanites for 20 years. Against him the Lord raised up Deborah, and when Jabin was killed she judged for 40 years. Sinning again, they were handed over to the Midianites for 7 years. Against these Gideon arose and judged the people for 40 years. After him his son judged for 3 years. After him Tola judged for 22 years. When Tola died, Jair was chosen by the people, and he too judged the people for 22 years. After his death the people sinned, and they were handed over to the Ammonites for 18 years; and when they cried to the Lord out of their distress, he raised up Jephthah for them, and he judged for 6 years. And Sebon judged for 7 years. Then the people sinned, and they were handed over to the foreigners for 40 years. When they turned again to the Lord, he raised up Samson for them, who, having defeated the foreigners, judged for 20 years. When he died, Shamgar judged for 1 year. After him the people were at peace, and there was no ruler over them; but each did what pleased him, and they were their own judges for 30 years.

IX. When these years had passed, then, Eli the priest judged for 20 years. He was succeeded by Samuel, himself also a priest of God, and he judged for 40 years, until he anointed Saul king. So all the years come to 561, as we said. As for those who think the Apostle related something else about these years, let them observe more carefully that those who wrote out the history of the years did not observe that the times of the Judges alone, set apart (as the Apostle did) without the years of captivity, are 111 years [fewer]. So all the years from the making of the world to Samuel, who anointed Saul king, are 4300. Then followed the times of the Kings. They had Kings for 514 years, from Saul to Zedekiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar, having put out his eyes, killed in the mill-house. The years of the Kings are then verified thus. Saul reigned 40 years, David reigned 40 years and 3 months, Solomon 40 years, Rehoboam 17 years, Abijah 3 years, Asa 41 years, Jehoshaphat 25 years, Joram 8 years, Ahaziah 1 year, Godolias 6 years, Joash 40 years, Amaziah 29 years, Uzziah 52 years, Jotham 17 years, Ahaz 15 years, Hezekiah 29 years, Manasseh 55 years, Amon 2 years, Josiah 31 years, Jehoahaz 3 months, Jehoiakim 11 years, Jehoiachin 3 months and 20 days, Zedekiah 11 years. So, as we said, the years of the Kings are 514.

X. From the making of the world, that is, to Zedekiah, when Jerusalem was overthrown and the people was carried away to Babylon, there are 4814 years. So after the eleventh year of Zedekiah, Jerusalem having been overthrown by King Nebuchadnezzar, the Jewish people was carried away into the Babylonian captivity. This captivity lasted 70 years; how these years were completed is shown clearer than light when from here we come to the weeks of Daniel, so that it may be most carefully verified from what time and where these weeks were completed. For Daniel, in his tenth vision, when he was wholly intent in prayer to God with attentive mind and anxious suspense, wishing to know whether the state of Jerusalem and its people would suffer any further harm from enemies after the Babylonian captivity, an angel of God appeared to him, saying: 'Daniel, I have now come forth to show you understanding; for the Lord's command went out, and I have come to make it plain to you; for you are a man of desires. Consider therefore the command, and understand the vision. Seventy weeks are cut off upon your people and upon the city of Jerusalem' (Dan. 9:22–24).

XI. So the angel marks out for Daniel both the total in seventy weeks, and in turn divides them in their order, [showing] when and how they are to be completed. And the angel continues on the same matter, saying thus: 'To blot out what they had received, and to bring sins to an end, and to make supplication for injustices, and to abolish offences, and to devise everlasting justice, and that vision and prophecy may be sealed, and that the Holy of Holies may be anointed; and be at rest and understand concerning the outcome of the Holy Ones, or the command to be answered and the city of Jerusalem to be built, until Christ the leader, seven weeks' (Dan. 9:24–25). These weeks are 49 years, and these years belong to the body of the 70 years of the captivity of Jerusalem. For in the first year of King Darius, who came to reign over the kingdom of the Chaldeans and who also killed King Belshazzar, Daniel saw the vision; and it was the 21st year of the captivity of Jerusalem. For Nebuchadnezzar lived 18 years after he had despoiled Zedekiah and Jerusalem, and his son Belshazzar reigned 3 years, in which third year he was killed, and Darius took over the kingdom. In his first year Daniel is told by the angel about the seventy weeks; and in dividing them, seven weeks were first named by the same angel, which (as has been said) are forty-nine years; these are joined to the 21 [years] of captivity when Daniel saw the vision, and they make seventy years, which were completed in Babylonia, so that the vision and prophecy of Jeremiah might be fulfilled. After these years Cyrus, king of the Persians, in the first year of his reign, ordered the peoples to go to Jerusalem, so that Jerusalem could be built and the Holy of Holies be anointed, which was the most sacred [place] in the Temple of God.

XII. So the peoples return from Babylonia, having with them as leader Zerubbabel, of whom mention was made by the angel to Daniel: 'until christ the leader, seven weeks'. For every king of the people of God is called christ in the divine law. For the prophet Zechariah too, [calling] him the future King, speaks thus to the people, saying: 'The hands of Zerubbabel have founded this house, and his hands will complete it, and you will know that the Lord almighty has sent me to you; for who has despised you in the days of small things? And they will rejoice in you, and will see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel' (Zech. 4:9–10); which emperors today are seen to carry in the right hand, as though [carrying] the people. The angel resumes and speaks to Daniel of 62 weeks [for] the Lord, that is, in which, the temple and the city of Jerusalem having been restored, they served the Lord with their offerings. These 62 weeks are 434 years, and these years were completed in the times of the Maccabees, in the 141st year of the kingdom of the Greeks. For at that time Antiochus reigned over the Greeks with a proud mind.

XIII. And although this order of years of the divine law, from the establishment of the world, is sufficient in itself, nevertheless, so that we may be seen to satisfy the reader's mind, running also through the kings of the Persians, we show from the histories of public records that from Cyrus the 62 weeks were fulfilled at this time of the Maccabees. For Cyrus reigned over the Persians 30 years, Artaxerxes reigned 9 years, Argus reigned 9 months, Darius reigned 36 years, Artaxerxes the second reigned 19 years and 2 months, Socidanus 7 months, Xerxes the elder son reigned 20 years, Artaxerxes reigned 72, Artabus reigned 7 months, Darius Nothus reigned 29 years, Olus reigned 22 years, Arser reigned 17 years, Darius reigned 6 years. Him Alexander the Great of Macedon killed; from whose time the history of the Maccabees [...] runs through the years of the Greeks in the divine narrative. So the whole total of the years of the kings of the Persians comes to 263; and from Alexander of Macedon to the times of Antiochus, that is, to the 141st year of the kingdom of the Greeks, the 62 weeks, that is 434 years, were completed (as we said).

XIV. 'After 62 weeks,' says the angel, 'the anointing and the holy things will be destroyed.' So after 7 and 62 weeks one week remains, which 7 years make up, to complete the total of 70 weeks. In this week, namely, the wickedness of the nations grew, just as had already been said by the angel; so that also in the middle of the same week the sacrifice is taken away from the holy place by Antiochus, king of the Greeks; and the Holy itself was polluted with womanish contempt, and the Abomination of desolation was set over the altar, and a statue of Jupiter, whom they call Olympian, was placed there. This Antiochus too, bearing with perverse mind the image of Antichrist, tried to make one people, one sacrilegious nation, under his rule. For he also allowed apostate men to build a gymnasium, that is, a place of training, in Jerusalem; and where God almighty had commanded a temple to be set up for himself only for praying to him and for offering holy sacrifices to him, he longed to pollute it with spectacles of idols.

XV. So when the 7 and 62 weeks had been completed, in this first week (as was said above) he ordered the Jewish nation to burn the books of the law, to sacrifice to images, and to eat unclean things; and this lasted until the twenty-fifth day of the 9th month in the 148th year of the kingdom of the Greeks, in which year all the 70 weeks are completed which the angel, running through them, set out for Daniel concerning the troubling of the city of Jerusalem and the overthrow of the people; about which matter Daniel himself, longing [to know], had also inquired of the Lord.

XVI. From here to the 174th year of the kingdom of the Greeks, at which time Lucius Licinius Lucullus, who was consul of the Romans, sent a letter concerning alliance and friendship to Simon, brother of Judas Maccabaeus, there are 26 years. And from his consulship, going through the yearly consuls, we find that up to the passion of our Lord Jesus Christ, up to the sixteenth year of the rule of Tiberius Caesar, 179 years were completed; and thus from the making of the world to the passion of Christ our Saviour there are 5530 years. Accordingly, 470 years are owing to complete six thousand years. For it must be that, just as the children of Israel, after the pledge made by the Lord God to Abraham, received the land of promise after 470 years, so we Christians too, after the same number of years, will have the first resurrection. For the Jewish people bears our figure in all things: 'On whom the ends of the ages have come' (1 Cor. 10:11). Therefore from the passion of the Lord Christ (from which time the Son of God promised resurrection to those who believe in him by faith) 470 years must be completed, so that the total of six thousand years may be concluded. At the beginning of the thousand-and-seventh year, those who believe with true faith will be freed from the world; for then will be the first resurrection of all the Saints.

XVII. Of the four hundred and seventy years from the passion of the Lord, 369 years have passed by the consulship of Caesarius and Atticus, on the ninth day before the Kalends of April. So 101 years remain for the 6000 years to be completed; and these 6000 years will not be completed unless first, near the last, ten kings have come forth into the world and have removed from the midst of the world the daughter of Babylon who now holds power. Against them there will suddenly come forth one mighty over them, who is named the Dragon in the Apocalypse, and he will master the ten kings; some of them he will destroy, others will remain under his dominion. 'Then that impious one will be revealed, the son of perdition, who is exalted against everything that is called God or that is worshipped, so that sitting in the temple of God he shows himself as if he were God himself' (2 Thess. 2:3–4). He will be the Antichrist proper. To him that most mighty Dragon, to whom the ten kings yielded, will hand over his strength and power, and all mortals will marvel. And the times of Antichrist will be (and these times must needs be mortal ones) like those when Antiochus tried to make one people in apostasy under his rule; but to him, since the time had not [come], such things did not happen as Antichrist will try to bring about. When he comes, he will come for the destruction of the unbelieving; his time will be grievous and abominable; and the Lord Christ alone will kill him with the breath of his mouth, and will bring him to nothing by the presence of his coming (ibid. 2:8).

XVIII. So when Antichrist has been overcome and killed, and the total of six thousand years completed, there will be the resurrection of all the saints while the world still survives; and a thousand years will also run their course, in which that ancient dragon (Rev. 20:2–3), the devil and Satan, bound in the abyss, will be shut away so that he may not lead anyone astray, until the years are completed; and these years will be counted for those who will remain under the sign of Antichrist, and all these will marry and be given in marriage, and will die. Upon them too will come those plagues described in the Apocalypse, and this world is struck down part by part again and again. For to the Saints of God there will be one day in the resurrection; and this day of the Saints will be extended in light as long as a thousand years will be counted for the impious who live in the world in punishment. This is the seventh day, the eternal and true sabbath, whose image and figure is held by the temporal sabbath written down in the law of Moses. For just as it was said to the Jewish people: 'Six days do the works of the world; but on the seventh day, which is called the sabbath, rest from your works' (Exod. 23:12), so for all the saints who have been from the beginning of the world, and those who now believe in Christ with true faith, once the six days (that is, six thousand years) have passed, in which they had toil and torment, the seventh day and true sabbath comes.

XIX. For this reason the Lord Christ forewarned every soul in the Gospel that one must hasten to believe in him beforehand, not at the time when eternal punishment must be rendered to the impious and good reward to the saints according to the merits of each: 'Pray,' he says, 'that your flight may not be in winter or on the sabbath' (Matt. 24:20). After the thousand-and-seventh year Satan will be loosed from his prison, and will go out to lead astray the nations Gog and Magog, and gather them against the camp of the Saints as if to fight; and fire will come down from heaven, and all men will be consumed; and then there will be the second resurrection for all flesh; and all will be judged by the just judgement of God, because they did not believe, but pleased themselves in their own righteousness. And after this, this heaven and this earth will be taken away; and that city which is described in the Apocalypse will come down from heaven prepared, with the riches of God, in which the just will dwell; and there will be a new heaven and a new earth, and both will remain for ever: the impious in eternal burning, but the just with God in eternal life. Amen.
